title: Disabled links and sides, block inheritance, and enforced links above a block

provenance.note: Documented Windows behavior (disabled link applies nothing; disabled side contributes nothing to that scope; block inheritance stops higher containers; enforced defeats the block and wins final precedence). WI-029 2026-08-04: the single HKCU assertion moved to the user-side-disabled scenario so this one could run under WP-6B's computer scope; the assertion was relocated, not dropped.

operator_meaning: The child OU blocks inheritance, so the plain domain GPO must not reach it
The enforced domain GPO must reach it anyway and win the conflict
The computer side of a user-side-disabled GPO must still apply
The disabled link must make its GPO vanish entirely

denied.reason: blocked by inheritance block on ou-studio-child

winners.reason: enforced links apply after non-enforced and win conflicts, and defeat block inheritance
computer side still applies when only the user side is disabled
CONTROL: unconflicted and unfiltered. Absent means the experiment did not run.

derivations: Block inheritance on a container stops GPOs linked above it, except enforced links; enforced links also apply last in precedence order and therefore win conflicts.
A disabled link removes the GPO from the applied set for that container; a disabled side removes only that scope's contribution.
Where Windows exposes a filtering reason in gpresult (disabled link, blocked), the harness records it verbatim; reason text is evidence, not a normalized field.

open_questions: Which exact reason strings does WS2025 gpresult report for inheritance-blocked versus link-disabled GPOs? Recorded verbatim at first execution; Studio's model must map to the reported category, not the string.

rsop.py PREDICTS Block=child (the OU-linked GPO wins) where this scenario expects Block=domainEnforced, and it omits the disabled-link GPO from its result entirely rather than reporting it denied. Both disagreements are recorded before execution; Windows arbitrates.
